transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM); Samira Khan (Acme Procurement), Luis Ortega (Acme Legal), Tom Nguyen (Acme Eng), David Price (Acme Security)

Summary: Brief procurement/legal kickoff to progress MSA/DPA review, confirm SLA expectations, pricing approvals and next steps for vendor onboarding. Redwood to provide compliance artifacts; Acme to return redline and onboarding questionnaire.

Topics: MSA clauses, DPA/data residency, SLAs/uptime, pricing & reserved capacity, onboarding checklist, SOC2 and security docs, timeline to contract/PO.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I'm Jordan, AE on the account, Priya our solutions engineer and Maya from success.
[00:05] Samira Khan: Hi all, Samira here, procurement. We've got Luis from legal and Tom on the line as well.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hi, everyone. Thanks for scheduling. We wanted to walk through the MSA and DPA next steps and answer any questions on SLAs and the onboarding flow.
[00:20] Luis Ortega: Great. We did a quick read of the draft you sent last week. A few things: limitation of liability, data retention, and subprocessing notices. Also need clarity on indemnification for third-party data claims.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: Totally. We're happy to take a look at your redlines. Our standard MSA has a mutual indemnity section but we can discuss caps tied to the fees. One note - the MSA references the DPA which is included as Appendix A in our package.
[00:48] David Price: On the DPA, can you confirm data residency options? Some of our manufacturing telemetry is EU-personal data, need EU residency and KMS control.
[00:58] Priya Singh: Yes. We support region pinning on the hosted model and dedicated/private deployments for full residency. For KMS, we have KMS integrations and on-prem HSM options. Apologies if I say K-V cash earlier in other calls, that's our KV cache, sorry for the slur.
[01:15] Tom Nguyen: For private deployment, we have to understand network requirements — IP ranges, VPC peering, and whether Redwood's private control plane needs inbound rules.
[01:24] Priya Singh: We'll provide a network diagram. For VPC deployments, the control plane is customer-managed in our Private offering; we supply the package and the orchestration. There may be one small outbound connection for updates but it's configurable.
[01:36] Luis Ortega: SLA language: uptime and credits. Our legal likes 99.95% for critical endpoints and clear remedies. Do you provide any credits or service levels for dedicated pools?
[01:48] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated, we provide SLA-backed latency and uptime targets in the enterprise contract. Credits are standard, with increased SLAs for reserved capacity. We'll include the SLA matrix in the SOW.
[01:58] Samira Khan: Pricing approvals: I need an official pricing sheet to run through procurement. Also need to know what commit levels trigger discounts and how burst capacity is handled in the pricing model.
[02:10] Priya Singh: Our pricing doc will show per-token for hosted, and reserved capacity tiers for Dedicated with burst options. Discounts kick in at monthly commit thresholds; we'll attach the chart. There's also an Optimize bundle for batching/quantization savings.
[02:23] Tom Nguyen: One technical question — how do you handle failovers? If a model variant can't serve, do you have automatic fallbacks to a smaller variant? That affects our continuity plan.
[02:33] Priya Singh: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and region fallback. There are policies we can tune per-route. We'll include the routing policy examples in the security doc pack.
[02:45] Luis Ortega: On subprocessing, do you list cloud providers? Our legal requires a subprocessors list for the DPA.
[02:52] Jordan Lee: We'll share the subprocessors list — it's included in the DPA package. Also will include our SOC 2 Type II report and an SOC2 summary.
[03:01] David Price: Can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit and the KMS controls for customer-managed keys?
[03:08] Priya Singh: All traffic is TLS; data at rest is encrypted. For Private and dedicated we support bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations and can supply HSM options for the on-prem package.
[03:20] Samira Khan: Procurement timeline — once we get the redline back and security docs, we need legal sign-off and then PO issuance. We're aiming for a March 1st start date for a pilot but procurement needs to clear budgets.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: That timeline seems reasonable. We'll aim to get docs over this week. Also, Maya will coordinate onboarding steps and the questionnaire.
[03:42] Maya Patel: I'll send the vendor onboarding checklist, include questions on SOC2, data flows, expected query volumes and a contact matrix for SSO/SAML setup.
[03:50] Tom Nguyen: For SSO, we use Okta and will need SCIM provisioning. Do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[03:58] Priya Singh: Yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll include the SSO integration guide.
[04:06] Luis Ortega: A couple of redline specifics: limitation of liability cap should be equal to fees paid in prior 12 months; also need a clearer termination for convenience clause.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: We can propose language that ties caps to fees and discuss termination notice. Jordan: noted — we'll propose edits in the redline.
[04:25] Samira Khan: Also need insurance certificates and any subcontractor attestations.
[04:30] Priya Singh: We'll attach our insurance summary and the list of subprocessors and whether subproc disclosure is available.
[04:38] Luis Ortega: Data retention: need clear retention buckets and deletion guarantees after termination — with confirmation timeline.
[04:46] Priya Singh: Standard retention windows are configurable by customer; for Private you control retention. We'll include deletion SLA timelines in the DPA sample.
[04:55] Tom Nguyen: On the engineering side, we'll want to run a short performance benchmark on our sample workload. How do we request benchmarking access?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: We can set up a POC with a dedicated sandbox and provide benchmark guidance. For procurement, would that be conditioned on a signed NDA or MSA?
[05:12] Samira Khan: We typically need a mutual NDA before sharing proprietary workloads.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Understood — we'll attach our mutual NDA and once that's signed we can start the POC.
[05:24] Luis Ortega: Also, please confirm data residency controls and whether logs/audit trails include token-level access for investigations.
[05:33] Priya Singh: Audit logs are available; we can provide token-level breakdowns in the Console and export logs for SIEM. We'll include that in the security pack.
[05:41] David Price: One more: retention of logs for X months — can you support 12 months?
[05:46] Priya Singh: We can support 12 months in enterprise observability add-on; we'll note pricing for extended retention.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: Okay, to recap — action items: Jordan sends redlined MSA & SOW, Priya sends SOC2/DPA/subprocessors + network diagrams, Maya sends onboarding checklist, Acme to return redline and complete onboarding questionnaire, schedule legal-only sync next week. Anyone disagree?
[06:09] Samira Khan: Sounds good. Luis: yes. Tom: good.
[06:14] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the legal-only call and the procurement checklist. Thanks everyone.
[06:20] End of call.

Notes about transcription: occasional mishearing in speech-to-text (e.g., K-V cash -> KV cache). Some speaker labels simplified. References to internal docs: link placeholders - [MSA draft link], [DPA sample link], [SOC2 report link], [Pricing matrix link], [Onboarding checklist link].
